A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same DriveTransformer research work, with readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F. Pages 3–17 have identical extracted text and rendered appearance; differences are confined to pages 1–2.

before.justification: v1 reports original Bench2Drive and nuScenes evaluations, model and task-head ablations, robustness tests, and additional experiments in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results, including benchmark comparisons, Dev10 experiments, robustness evaluations, and the appendix training-stage analysis.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains identical tokenization, sensor/task/temporal attention, FIFO memory, task heads, training losses, and inference procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Bench2Drive/CARLA and nuScenes coverage, Dev10 subset, driving tasks, and camera-corruption scenarios. No datasets or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the experiments, including UniAD and VAD in the main comparisons and ParaDrive, SparseAD, and SparseDrive in Appendix E.

E3.justification: The training data, 220-route main evaluation, Dev10 ablations, validation sets, metrics, model configurations, and corruption procedures remain identical in Section 4 and Appendices A–B.

E4.justification: The scaling study in Figure 7, ablations in Tables 5–6, robustness analyses in Tables 7–8, and training-stage analysis in Appendix F are unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix B reports the same three-seed Dev10 evaluation in both versions. No run-count disclosure, uncertainty-reporting practice, or statistical procedure changes.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings are identical, including the appendix comparisons. For example, Table 1 retains DriveTransformer-Large's driving score of 63.46 and success rate of 35.01%.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations (1)–(7) are unchanged. Neither version contains additional theoretical propositions or proofs absent from the other.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about task parallelism, sparse representation, streaming processing, training stability, scalability, and benchmark performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations of scaling, training stability, and robustness are unchanged. Appendix C retains the same limitation concerning coupled subtask updates and system maintenance.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains identical implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, image resolution, and memory-queue settings. The repository link and stated plans to release code, checkpoints, and Dev10 are unchanged.

R1.justification: The citations, bibliography, related-work discussion, and positioning against sequential, parallel, and sparse autonomous-driving methods remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The first author's name changes from Xiaosng Jia to Xiaosong Jia. The affiliation block removes Shanghai AI Lab and its numbering, and a corresponding-author affiliation footnote is added. Scientific prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The revised author block and footnote shift first-page content, including Figure 1, and move the opening two introduction lines from page 2 to page 1. The version/date stamp also changes; figure and table contents remain identical.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects an author-name typo and updates affiliations, with limited layout changes. The scientific narrative, methods, empirical evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information—including all appendices—remain unchanged, establishing no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
